notes: The C implementation uses a prototype-stage global registry `priv_list` to map CPUs to shared private_data clusters.
The Rust candidate should not mechanically copy the global registry shape.
Long-lived frequency-policy resources are better modeled as per-policy state.
Probe/device state should remain a light descriptor plus shared configuration, not the owner of policy resources.

allowed_owner_adjustments: Move long-lived cpumask, OPP regulator token, OPP table, cpufreq table, and clk ownership from the global `private_data` list entry into a per-policy Rust owner.
Keep a lightweight platform/shared-config owner for cluster discovery and driver registration data.
must_stay_semantically_equivalent: One logical policy owner per shared CPU mask.
The related CPU mask visible through cpufreq policy must match the C sharing semantics.
Frequency transitions must continue to read the selected frequency entry and call into the OPP rate setter for the primary CPU device.
Probe/remove and init/exit pairings must preserve the same acquisition and release coverage as the C baseline.

private_data.role: Cluster-level resource bundle and registry node shared across all CPUs in one policy.

priv_list.role: Global registry used to locate the cluster owner by CPU membership.

cpufreq_policy.role: Per-policy view that receives cpus, clk, freq_table, suspend_freq, transition latency, and driver_data.

cpufreq_driver.role: Static driver instance whose callbacks are optionally patched by platform data before registration.

mutations: expand to shared CPUs via OPP sharing lookup
fallback can widen to all CPUs before setting sharing
cpumask.release: free_cpumask_var in dt_cpufreq_release or early_init rollback

cpu_device.attach: stored in private_data and later reused by set_target, cpufreq_init, and release paths
cpu_device.release: borrowed core device pointer; no explicit put in this driver

opp_regulator_token.release: dev_pm_opp_put_regulators in dt_cpufreq_release or early_init rollback

opp_table.acquire: dev_pm_opp_of_cpumask_add_table when static OPP data is present

freq_table.attach: stored in private_data then published to policy->freq_table in cpufreq_init

cpufreq_dt_find_data.purpose: Map a CPU id to the private_data cluster by scanning the registry.

find_supply_name.purpose: Resolve the legacy `cpu0-supply` versus modern `cpu-supply` regulator naming.

set_target.purpose: Read policy->freq_table[index] and set the OPP rate for the cluster's CPU device.

notes: init acquires clk late and publishes the cluster resources into policy
exit only releases clk; cluster resources remain owned by the global registry until driver unregister/remove

dt_cpufreq_early_init.purpose: Create a cluster owner for a CPU if none exists, discover related CPUs, set regulators, load OPP tables, and build the cpufreq frequency table.

dt_cpufreq_release.purpose: Destroy every cluster owner and release freq tables, static OPP tables, regulator token, cpumask, and registry membership.

notes: probe iterates all present CPUs and runs early init before registering the cpufreq driver
probe mutates the static cpufreq_driver based on optional cpufreq_dt_platform_data
remove unregisters the driver and then releases all cluster resources

cpufreq_dt_pdev_register.purpose: Exported helper that allows provider drivers to create the cpufreq-dt platform device as a child of their device.

platdev_autocreation.purpose: Core-initcall path that creates the cpufreq-dt platform device for allowlisted machines or OPP-v2 systems not in the blocklist.
platdev_autocreation.runtime_note: This is the generic standalone creation seam and is distinct from provider-assisted `cpufreq_dt_pdev_register`.

shared_mask_source: fallback to dev_pm_opp_get_sharing_cpus, then cpumask_setall plus dev_pm_opp_set_sharing_cpus
policy_visibility: cpufreq_dt_find_data relies on membership in the same mask
sharing_semantics.implication_for_rust: Per-policy ownership may replace the registry shape, but related CPU mask results must stay equivalent.

error_rollback_and_drop_pairs.failure: empty OPP table or cpufreq table init failure

error_rollback_and_drop_pairs.pairing: clk_get/clk_put is per-policy; OPP/freq-table/regulator/cpumask teardown is registration-lifetime

kbuild_switching.note: Current-tree already provides the primary CPUFREQ_DT versus CPUFREQ_DT_RUST switch, but ARM_IMX_CPUFREQ_DT is still tied only to CPUFREQ_DT in Kconfig.arm.
